name: BACH_0250
markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests InSitu (68%)** · Ambiguous: Normal vs InSitu · Careful review
Two-class conformal set, flagged reliability, and second-model disagreement.

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | InSitu 68%, Normal 32% | Leading, not decisive |
| Conformal set | Normal, InSitu | Cannot separate the two |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.70 / 88th percentile | Input flagged |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Models disagree |
| Similar cases | 1 of 5 InSitu | Neighbors mostly Normal |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor cell fraction** (regions 3, 4, 5) · context · 73% neoplastic nuclei, above 97% of references [F7] · Measured
- **Benign fibrous stroma or fat** (regions 9, 10, 11) · ↓ invasive · Associated with lower invasive likelihood [F3] · Validated
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 11) · ↑ invasive · Small positive term; invasive risk stays 0.2% [F4] · Validated
- **Normal lobules** (regions 3, 10, 11) · ↓ invasive · Strongest negative term; spot check 0/20 [F2] · Unreliable

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing top 3 regions drops invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI (−0.005 to 0.007) includes 0; unproven. Case leans on Unreliable normal lobules.

## Could be wrong if
- Image is atypical (OOD 88th percentile), so all probabilities may be off.
- Heatmap and concepts address invasive risk, not Normal vs InSitu; that split is unexplained.

## Check on the slide
1. **Region 5**: 169 neoplastic nuclei counted; judge in situ versus benign architecture.
2. **Region 11**: is the infiltrating stroma true invasion or periductal stroma?
3. **Region 6**: look for atypical cells confined within ducts (12/20 spot check).
